context.in_practice: Nothing in these tests tells the two routes apart. Every implementation on both routes reads the first key correctly, keeps the BOM when it writes the file back, and makes the same edits. All of them also turn the two spaces before an end-of-line comment into one. Route 2 never considered the BOM, but it still handled it the same way.
context.stakes: Some config files start with an invisible byte-order mark (BOM), which Windows editors often add. When a file like that is read and edited, the user can lose the mark, get the first key read wrongly (for example as "\ufeffmodel" instead of "model"), or see the edit land in the wrong place in the file.
context.tradeoff: Route 1 deliberately keeps the BOM in the text, so where comments and edits land in the file stays correct. Route 2 never addressed the BOM and costs nothing extra; it behaved the same in this run, but nothing in it guarantees that.

plan_why: Config files and an included file that start with a UTF-8 BOM, where the first line has an end-of-line comment. The commands check whether the first key can still be read, whether a set keeps the BOM (or drops or doubles it), and whether the comment stays in the same column after a set.
routes: Decode as plain UTF-8 so the BOM stays in the text and is written back unchanged
